authority_note: This checkpoint does not replace companies/PWR/latest.json or the current canonical 2026-09-06 assessment. Promotion requires a canonical deep run.
thesis: Quanta is showing unusually strong secular demand, execution and backlog growth across grid modernization, power delivery, data-center and large-load infrastructure. The principal underwriting issue has shifted from demand validation to capital-allocation quality: whether an acquisition-heavy strategy and rising debt can produce durable post-tax incremental returns comfortably above the 9% hurdle while preserving per-share free-cash-flow compounding.

evidence: Q2 2026 filing identifies multi-year grid modernization, transmission/substation expansion, data-center load growth, reshoring and electrification as demand drivers.
Backlog reached $53.44B at June 30, 2026, up 21.5% from December 31, 2025; RPO reached $33.55B, up 41.2%.
Q2 consolidated revenue grew 41.1% and operating income 87.6%, with both reportable segments expanding margins.
counter_evidence: Part of growth is acquisition-driven and the infrastructure cycle remains exposed to project timing, regulation, weather and customer capital budgets.
Electric represents roughly 82% of H1 revenue, so the structural thesis is concentrated in power-related infrastructure.

evidence: Services are mission-critical for power delivery, grid reliability, load-center infrastructure, utility systems and recurring maintenance.
No customer represented 10% or more of consolidated revenue in H1 2026 or H1 2025, reducing single-customer dependency.
Quanta's breadth across engineering, procurement, construction, maintenance and specialized craft labor supports a total-solutions proposition.
counter_evidence: MSAs often do not commit customers to specific volumes.
Project awards remain competitively bid and can be deferred, resized or cancelled.

evidence: Backlog and RPO are expanding while segment margins improve, consistent with stronger demand and execution rather than pure low-margin volume growth.
Quanta combines geographic scale, specialized labor, utility relationships and cross-discipline execution capabilities that are difficult to assemble quickly.
Q2 Electric margin improved to 11.5% from 10.1%; Underground and Infrastructure improved to 9.1% from 6.9%.
counter_evidence: The moat is execution- and labor-based rather than protected by a proprietary product monopoly.
Large complex projects carry fixed-price and change-order risk; aggressive bidding can impair realized economics.

evidence: Calculated simple FCF was about $1.62B in 2025, versus $1.48B in 2024 and $1.14B in 2023; the two-year CAGR was about 19.2%.
Calculated FY2025 simple FCF per diluted share was about $10.71, up despite modest diluted-share growth.
H1 2026 calculated simple FCF was about $1.04B, versus $0.27B in H1 2025.
counter_evidence: H1 2026 OCF benefited from an approximately $455M favorable year-over-year working-capital swing, so current cash growth should not be annualized mechanically.
2025 acquisition cash spend was about $3.05B and H1 2026 added roughly $1.09B of cash consideration plus shares; cohort-level post-close ROIC is not yet established.
August 2026 added $2.0B of senior notes and the supplied filing does not establish the use-of-proceeds bridge.

evidence: Long-term incentive metrics explicitly include ROIC, cumulative adjusted EPS and relative TSR; the CEO and President-Electric have 70% of LTI tied to performance measures.
The company has continued dividends and maintains a $1.0B repurchase authorization as of June 30, 2026.
Management has expanded capabilities into mechanical, civil and large-load-center infrastructure aligned with identified customer demand.
counter_evidence: Capital allocation is acquisition-heavy and increasingly debt-funded, which raises the burden of proof on integration and incremental returns.
The proxy discloses related-party facility leases and family employment involving certain executives/directors; these are disclosed and subject to policy but merit ongoing governance monitoring.
H1 2026 had no common-stock repurchases while share count edged higher.

evidence: H1 2026 operating cash flow was $1.49B and June 2026 available credit commitments plus cash were about $2.77B.
No customer was 10% or more of consolidated revenue or receivables in the disclosed H1 periods.
FY2025 financial statements received an unqualified audit opinion and internal controls were effective; Q2 2026 disclosure controls were also effective.
counter_evidence: Gross long-term debt obligations were about $6.10B at June 30, 2026 before the subsequent $2.0B senior-note issuance.
The company is capital intensive, expects $750M-$800M of 2026 capex and has material contractual, bonding, insurance and project obligations.
Fixed-price project errors, weather events or claim collection issues can create large cash and margin volatility.

evidence: No synchronized current quote and no 9% reverse DCF were included in this supplied-filings extraction.
counter_evidence: A strong business can still be a poor investment if the market price requires an unrealistic continuation of current growth and margins.
missing_data: Synchronized share price and enterprise value
Pro-forma net debt after August 2026 notes

evidence: Grid modernization, data-center power demand, reshoring and electrification create a multi-year opportunity set with large addressable infrastructure spend.
Backlog growth and expanding margins provide operating leverage if execution remains strong.
counter_evidence: Construction economics are ultimately bounded by labor, project risk and capital intensity; upside is less unconstrained than a software-like model.
M&A and leverage can convert a favorable demand cycle into permanent capital impairment if integration returns disappoint.

evidence: PwC issued unqualified FY2025 financial-statement and ICFR opinions.
Q2 2026 disclosure controls were reported effective.
Related-party transactions are disclosed and subject to an Audit Committee approval policy; they remain a monitoring item rather than an integrity failure on current evidence.
The company generates substantial operating cash flow and had about $2.77B of available commitments plus cash at June 30, 2026.
External capital is being used for growth, acquisitions and capital structure management rather than to fund a structurally cash-negative core business.
items.monitor: The August $2.0B note issuance materially increases financing obligations; pro-forma leverage still needs reconciliation.

evidence: Shares outstanding rose about 0.47% from year-end 2025 to June 30, 2026; this is not yet persistent/fatal dilution.
The company retains a $1.0B repurchase authorization.
items.monitor: Acquisition-share issuance and SBC should be tracked against FCF-per-share growth; diluted weighted-average shares rose about 0.9% year over year in H1.

evidence: Q2 revenue grew 41.1% while consolidated operating margin expanded to 7.3% from 5.5%.
Both segments posted material operating-margin improvement.
Management-disclosed acquired-business revenue explains only about one-third of Q2 revenue growth on a rough bridge, indicating a large non-acquisition growth component.
items.monitor: H1 cash conversion was helped by working capital and acquisition contributions are meaningful, so organic cash economics need multi-period confirmation.

evidence: 2025 acquisition cash spend was about $3.05B; H1 2026 added about $1.09B cash plus equity consideration; another acquisition closed after June quarter-end.
August 2026 added $2.0B of senior notes at 4.85%-5.55% coupons.
Current filings do not yet provide a clean post-close cohort ROIC/FCF bridge showing returns comfortably above the 9% hurdle.
items.resolution_needed: Build CEI, Dynamic Systems and 2026-deal post-close revenue/margin/FCF/ROIC cohorts and compare to 9% required return.

evidence: Backlog and RPO expanded sharply into June 2026 while Electric and Underground margins improved.
No evidence in supplied filings of customer concentration deterioration or broad project-loss pressure overwhelming growth.
items.monitor: Track bidding discipline, fixed-price losses, skilled-labor availability and margin retention.

evidence: No synchronized quote or reverse DCF is included in this checkpoint.
items.resolution_needed: Run a 9% reverse DCF and explicit Bear/Base/Bull valuation against current price and pro-forma net debt.

evidence: No customer represented 10% or more of disclosed H1 revenue or receivables.
Electric is about 82% of revenue, but it spans utilities, power generation, technology load centers and communications rather than a single customer/product dependency.
items.monitor: Power-infrastructure concentration remains a cyclical/regulatory exposure even if it is not currently fatal.

evidence: Business survival appears robust, but permanent-loss risk depends on valuation and whether acquisition-heavy reinvestment earns adequate returns after financing costs.
Fixed-price project losses and working-capital/claim collection can create cash shocks in an otherwise growing business.
items.resolution_needed: Combine valuation, post-August leverage and acquisition-cohort ROIC into a downside loss-of-capital case.

falsifiers: Backlog and RPO stop converting into revenue and cash while receivables, contract assets or claims structurally absorb cash.
Electric or Underground segment margins regress materially despite the current strong demand environment.
CEI, Dynamic Systems and 2026 acquisition cohorts fail to generate post-tax cash returns above the 9% hurdle after integration.
Debt-funded acquisitions push leverage/refinancing risk materially higher without commensurate per-share FCF growth.
Fixed-price losses, unapproved claims or change-order write-downs become persistent and material.
SBC and acquisition share issuance outpace repurchases and underlying FCF-per-share growth.
next_evidence: Synchronized current quote plus 9% reverse DCF and Bear/Base/Bull valuation
Acquisition cohort bridge for CEI, Dynamic Systems and 2026 deals: purchase price -> incremental revenue -> margin -> FCF -> post-tax ROIC
Exact use of proceeds and pro-forma net debt after August 2026 $2.0B note issuance
Backlog/RPO conversion and working-capital normalization across at least four quarters
Fixed-price contract mix, loss-project history, unapproved claim aging and realized collections
preliminary_conclusion: Primary filings materially strengthen the prior PWR screen: demand, backlog, margins, cash generation and governance are substantially better evidenced than in the 2026-09-06 preliminary record. PWR merits promotion to a P1 valuation/reinvestment-quality review, but no buy authorization is justified until the 9% price gate and acquisition-return/debt bridge are completed.
